content: Hydralazine is a medication that can cause a variety of side effects, ranging from common to serious. Below is a detailed explanation of these effects, precautions, and important considerations for its use. Common Side Effects of Hydralazine The most frequently reported side effects of hydralazine include: Headache: This is a common reaction and may vary in intensity. Decreased Appetite: Some individuals may experience a reduced desire to eat. Nausea and Vomiting: These gastrointestinal symptoms are relatively common. Diarrhea: Loose stools or increased bowel movements may occur. Pounding or Fast Heartbeat: Known as palpitations, this can be unsettling for some patients. Chest Pain or Discomfort: This may occur and should be monitored closely. If any of these side effects become bothersome or persistent, it is important to inform your healthcare provider. There may also be other side effects not listed here, so any unusual symptoms should be reported. Serious Side Effects of Hydralazine While less common, hydralazine can cause serious side effects that require immediate medical attention: Lupus-like Symptoms Hydralazine can induce symptoms resembling lupus, an autoimmune condition. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if you experience: Rash Joint pain Fever Weakness or unusual tiredness Swollen glands Reduced need to urinate Pink, red, or brown-colored urine Swelling in any part of the body Chest Pain Hydralazine may cause chest pain, which could be a sign of a heart attack. This risk is higher in individuals with pre-existing heart disease. Do not take hydralazine if you have recently had a heart attack without consulting your healthcare provider. Seek emergency medical help if you experience: Chest pain or pressure Fast or abnormal heartbeat Difficulty breathing Pain radiating to your back, jaw, throat, or arm Sweating, upset stomach, vomiting, or dizziness Blood Disorders Hydralazine can lead to blood-related complications, such as agranulocytosis (low neutrophil count), anemia, or leukopenia (low white blood cell count). Notify your healthcare provider immediately if you develop: Fever Shortness of breath Pale or yellowish skin Easy bruising or bleeding Frequent infections Unusual weakness or tiredness Dizziness, lightheadedness, or a feeling of faintness Headache Fast or irregular heartbeat Nerve Problems Hydralazine can cause peripheral neuropathy, which involves damage to the nerves that transmit signals between the body and the brain. Symptoms may include tingling, numbness, or weakness in the extremities. Precautions for Hydralazine Use Certain individuals should not use hydralazine due to specific health conditions or allergies: Allergies to Ingredients Do not use hydralazine if you are allergic to: Hydralazine itself Apresoline (a brand name for hydralazine) Any other ingredients in the specific product dispensed. Your pharmacist can provide a complete list of ingredients. Heart Disease Hydralazine is contraindicated in individuals with coronary artery disease (CAD), a condition where the arteries supplying blood to the heart are narrowed or blocked. Relaxation of blood vessels caused by hydralazine can increase the workload on the heart, potentially leading to a heart attack. Mitral Valvular Rheumatic Heart Disease Patients with mitral valve damage due to rheumatic fever should avoid hydralazine. The increased blood flow to the heart caused by the medication can strain the mitral valve and exacerbate heart function. Important Considerations Before Using Hydralazine Prescription Use Only: Hydralazine should only be taken if prescribed by a healthcare provider. Follow the prescribed dosage and instructions carefully. Do Not Share: Never share hydralazine with others, even if they have similar symptoms or conditions, as it may harm them. Keep Out of Reach of Children: Store hydralazine safely to prevent accidental ingestion by children. Impact on Alertness: Hydralazine may affect your coordination or alertness. Avoid driving or engaging in activities requiring full attention until you know how the medication affects you. Information to Share with Your Healthcare Provider Before starting hydralazine, inform your healthcare provider about: All current and past health conditions, including heart disease, kidney disease, stroke, or rheumatic fever. Any prescription or over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are taking. This helps prevent potential drug interactions. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding Pregnancy: The effects of hydralazine on pregnancy and unborn babies are not fully understood. Inform your healthcare provider if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. They will advise whether hydralazine is appropriate for you. Breastfeeding: Hydralazine passes into breast milk. Discuss with your healthcare provider if you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed. Drug and Food Interactions Food and Non-Alcoholic Drinks: There are no known interactions between hydralazine and food or non-alcoholic beverages. Alcohol: It is unclear how alcohol affects hydralazine, but drinking alcohol while on this medication may increase the risk of dizziness. Overdose and Missed Doses Overdose: If you or someone else has taken too much hydralazine, seek immediate medical attention, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take double or extra doses. How to Use Hydralazine Hydralazine is available in two forms: A liquid that is injected into a blood vessel or muscle. A tablet that is swallowed. Always follow your healthcare provider’s instructions regarding the form and dosage of hydralazine prescribed to you.
